protocol: Track P (#188, #247): one protocol version, the first since #27's scored batch on manifest v7, frozen at the commit recorded on #188. Its one change to the validity rules is C7 (tool_differences.nested_agents): a detected nested agent runtime makes the run invalid, hits are counted per arm, and the batch stops and asks on the first hit. Since #305 (manifest v38) the engine proposes no Split for joined agents while a pending offer exists (a checkpoint offer still available at its agent's current revision), so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since #311 (manifest v39) a pending review obligation is uncertain regrouping evidence only when the owners its cause edit names relate to the closure of the obligation's scope, so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since #355, #356 and #358 (manifest v44) a Falinks worker survives relocation at any point in a run (notices and developments kept, safety evidence kept, no peer stall), a published path overlaps a split workspace only if a published operation missing from it wrote it, capture can return the published side of an overlap, and a declined failure report no longer drives engine proposals, so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since manifest v45 a relocation's control failure is evidence control_failure, not nested_agent: the batch pause names it and the report counts control_failure_runs. Since #364 (manifest v46) regrouping's current work is each agent's unpublished drafts (its registered scopes only before it has edited and before any transition), a split whose agents' drafts relate by compiler closure is kept or, once agreed, refused as Stale (unsafe until publication), and for a join only an overlap between drafts or an overlapping publication is new evidence, so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since #335 (manifest v52) the Falinks host records a runtime line whose message is text, such as the permission_denied line a deny rule writes, instead of stopping on it (wave 1 lost its first run that way), so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since #335 (manifest v53) a declined join is not proposed again when only a pending offer or uncertainty changed (wave 1, run 3), so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since #335 (manifest v54) supersedes and withdraw also take the ID an offer's reply gave (every supersedes call in waves 1 and 2 named it and was refused), so Falinks-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions. Since #335 (manifest v55) a Git-arm check takes the resolved merge commit by an unambiguous short ID as well as the full one (the instructions never asked for the full ID; in local-evidence, 40 of the 75 checks that named a commit gave a short ID and were refused, in 31 Git runs), so Git-arm runs before and after it are different protocol versions; the engine and the Falinks arm are unchanged.

tool_differences.git: Two writable Git worktrees with native Read/Grep/Glob/Edit/Write and unsandboxed-by-Claude Bash inside the host sandbox-exec profile; host commands (message/share/ack/check/ready) via Bash; unfinished diffs; ordinary merges and conflict resolution; exact host-captured checks. The worker sandbox allows outbound network for the runtime, so Git-arm Bash also has network; Falinks-arm Bash runs in Claude Code's sandbox without it. No Falinks ledger or offer/reconsideration protocol.
tool_differences.falinks: Live group workspace read with native Read/Grep/Glob; source changes only through engine-mediated falinks tools (edits, revision-bound reviews, offers, feedback runs, regrouping, gofmt job) plus host ack/check/ready tools. Claude Code's own sandbox: Bash writes only scratch. Enrollment fixes the file set: fixture files except dot-paths (held by the host and added to every candidate) plus x_test.go / tests/x.rs per source file. Publication requires the engine's visible checks; host check/final readiness add the oracle.
tool_differences.shared: Same pinned Claude Code binary, model, --effort medium (`reasoning`), --max-turns 12 per message with host continuation, isolation flags, fresh sessions, allocation, requirements, dependency information, milestone triggers, peer-event delivery at presentation boundaries, two-minute idle reminders, pass/fail-only visible+oracle checks and 30-minute bound. No oracle/reference access.
tool_differences.team_size: Track T only (#178), Git arm: a team of one gets the solo prompt and instructions/git-solo.md (same requirements and check/ready protocol, no peer worktree, messages or diffs) and every allocation, A then B. Development texts are unchanged, so they still say "both agents" and "A:/B:". The solo development trigger is the observable rule of #5: the solo agent's own first share since the last development. Each run's events record when developments arrived and the drafts shared after them. The scored batch always runs teams of two.
tool_differences.nested_agents: Both arms (#178 C7): a Bash command whose first word is claude, codex, node, npx or the configured runtime binary, or a session in the worker's runtime project folder the host did not launch, makes the run invalid; the batch stops and asks. Not detected: a nested instance with its own HOME or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under scratch, an obfuscated launch, a direct API curl, a launch wrapped in another program (bash -c, xargs, sudo), and a session written outside the worker's own project folder (another cwd).
